entries.title: Remaining leads from the survey of comparable agent orchestrators (Oct 2026)
entries.body:
Leads borrowed from comparable open-source agent orchestrators, surveyed in October 2026 (first imported from issue #671).
Nothing here is a commitment; these are leads to triage.
The orch checked each against the code on 2026-11-17: ideas lym has built or that proved moot are dropped,
partly built ones name only what is still open, and the eight most worth doing are notes of their own in this project.
Each bullet names its source project and the lym module it would touch.

## Plan validation and concurrency (quarry, Plan-Write, board)

- **Typed scope operations on cards** (foremerge): each scope carries an additive or breaking operation,
  and deterministic rules flag colliding pairs even when files do not overlap.
  Worth comparing against board labels and the alignment gate.
- **Symbol leases between concurrent tasks** (Fusion, ORCH): expiring leases on symbol keys serialize overlapping tasks,
  with a deterministic tie-break; lym keeps overlapping tasks apart by board labels.
- **Commit-time reservation guard** (ntm): a pre-commit hook refuses a commit touching what another task holds; needs leases first.
- **Criterion amendment ledger** (oh-my-claudecode): a card's acceptance text changes only through a recorded amendment in weft.

## Review (burler, Bouncer)

- **Quorum of differently-angled judges** (ccswarm): lym fans out lenses but has no quorum vote for high-risk segments.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's parent orch can be asked to see and veto each Code-Review round and each drift judge ruling
  (`code_review_ask_parent`, `judge_ask_parent`); that is one extra judge, not a quorum.
- **Risk tier by changed paths** (yylo): globs over sensitive paths choose the review depth and the gate scope.

## Engine, recipes and governance (shed, tender, orch, board)

- **Cross-run quarantine** (Bernstein): a task that fails three times across runs is held, unless the failures were the host's.
- **Fork a run from a step with a tree snapshot** (Bernstein): `shed goto` moves the cursor but does not restore the warp tree.
- **Warm retry guarded by a workspace hash** (Bernstein): resume the native session only when the tree is unchanged.
- **Evidence reuse by input identity** (yylo): verify is skipped on the same tree; a changed review prompt could rerun only the review.
- **Guidance at the next step boundary** (Conductor): a queue of operator guidance for the next producer's prompt.
  Partly met since 2026-11-19: `notify_parent_on` in `loom.yaml` mails the run's parent when a named row is reached,
  so the parent can brief that row's agent as it starts; there is still no queue of guidance lym itself folds into the prompt.
- **Batched operator questions with recorded assumptions** (Spec Kit `/clarify`, Conductor): Discussion-Write asks at most a few ranked questions,
  each with a recommended answer, and records unanswered ones as assumptions.
  Since 2026-11-19 a run's autonomous agents put their questions to the run's parent orch, not to the operator in their pane;
  Discussion, which the operator sits in, still asks in its pane, so this lead concerns Discussion only.
- **Rate-limit wait**: the orch watcher wakes the orch after a usage reset; tender itself schedules no resume.
- **Standing goals and scheduled routines** (ORCH, CAO, Fusion): periodic triage, dependency bumps or `selfreport` sweeps.

## Agent sessions (reed, shuttle)

- **Waiting-for-input signal** (agent-of-empires): shuttle has an awaiting-input state; screen heuristics still decide readiness and startup.
- **Reference status patterns and a paste pitfall** (CAO): compare its regexes and its tmux bracketed-paste note with shuttle's readiness and creel inject.
- **Context forecasting** (ntm): the orch cycles its context; Webster's Master and the loom driver do not, and nothing forecasts.
- **Staggered spawns** (ntm): space Webster forks and batten fan-out by learned rate limits.

## Observability (report, weft)

- **Hash-chained run journal** (Bernstein): a hash chain over producer outputs makes an archived run self-verifying.
- **Unverified-completion rate** (Bernstein): a `lym report` view of completions with no test or gate behind them.
- **Commit-to-record links** (AgentNote): weft links to warp by a `Warp-SHA:` trailer; a note or trailer on each warp commit could link back.
- **Run diff** (ccswarm): `lym report` comparing two archived runs' timelines and token use.
- **OpenTelemetry spans per producer** (Conductor).

## Operator attention (orch, dobby, reed)

- **Attention feed with acknowledgement states** (ntm): dobby's wait reminders have no seen, snoozed or acknowledged states.

## Discussion review (Discussion-Write, stencils, pattern)

- **Requirements-quality checklist** (Spec Kit `/checklist`): items with IDs the Discussion-review judge answers one by one.
- **Fixed analysis categories** (Kiro): inconsistency, ambiguity, conflicts, unstated assumptions and missing edge cases as named lenses.
- **PATTERN rules handed to reviewers** (Spec Kit constitution): its rules as numbered MUSTs in plan and code review prompts.
- **Glob-scoped steering** (Kiro): stencils pull per-area guidance chosen by the paths of a plan's glyphs.

entries.title: A closed area for lym: bwrap sandbox in stages, off by default
entries.brief: Run the lym process tree in a bwrap area with a host proxy and broker, built in three stages with a stop; to be split if it goes ahead
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-10-30)

Every agent lym starts runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, which many people do not accept, and a repository that states it supports safe sandboxing is worth more than one that does not.
The area matters most on the work machine OSL-1046 (operator, 2026-11-22).
On OSL-1046 sudo is tightly limited and does not cover AppArmor, so the profile `bwrap` needs on Ubuntu 24.04 cannot be loaded there; a `bwrap` area, and podman or Claude Code's `/sandbox`, which need the same user namespaces, are blocked on that machine until IT loads it. Landlock needs no privilege and is the option left to weigh there.
The operator uses lym alone, on Linux (OSL-1046: Ubuntu 24.04; Neve: Kubuntu on Ubuntu 26.04, Plasma 6), and has no interest in other users or in Windows.
The research is `docs/research/platform/sandboxing-options-2026-10-30.md`: it weighs `bwrap`, Landlock, a dedicated Linux user, systemd sandboxing, podman and Claude Code's own `/sandbox`, and the packages and cards each would change.

Two exposures hold today with no area: an agent can reach `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and through it `systemd-run --user`, which starts any process outside lym's tree, and it can type into other hubs' tmux panes through their sockets in `/tmp/tmux-<uid>`, the Models hub's among them.

## Idea

Run the whole lym process tree inside a `bwrap` area launched by lym itself, with the agents free inside it and a short, controlled list of exits.
It is an option the operator turns on, never a requirement: with it off, everything works as it does today, and with it on, nothing starts when the sandbox cannot.
The operator thinks the full design is complicated and error-prone, and doubts it will work without large problems, so it is built in stages with a stop between them.
This is one large note and is split into tasks, or a project, only when the operator decides it goes ahead.

### Before the area: two cheap steps

- Start a hub's tmux server from a Konsole window, not a VS Code terminal: the server inherits the `vscode` AppArmor profile, which grants user namespaces to every agent of the hub.
- A line in `README.md` that every agent lym starts runs with bypass permissions, and that lym belongs on a machine the operator is willing to hand to its agents.

### Stage 1: the filesystem area only

`bwrap` with `--unshare-all --die-with-parent --clearenv` around reed's tmux server and everything under it, started by a new `lym area start` and a supervisor inside.

- The hub is bound read-write at its own path, since the tmux server name, the creel socket name, git's worktree links and Claude Code's transcript directory all derive from absolute paths; `/usr`, `/etc` and `/opt` are read-only, `$HOME` a tmpfs with read-only binds of the Go toolchain, the Claude Code binary and the installed `lym`.
- The area has its own Claude config directory and Go caches bound at the usual paths, with the host's plugin cache read-only on top, so the host's `settings.json` hooks never run in it.
- One host directory holds the tmux socket directory, so `lym reed attach` from outside drives the server inside; tried on OSL-1046 with a tmux server inside `bwrap`.
- `.git/hooks` is read-only; `.git/config` was to stay writable for `branch.<b>.lymLocal`, but `fabric-remote-async` removed that mark and `internal/gitrepo/branchmark.go`, so the reason is gone; whether git itself or another lym writer still needs `.git/config` writable is unchecked.
- Network stays open and there is no broker, so the landing deploy, `lym reed window`, `lym ide` and `lym hibernate request` do not work from inside; the operator does them by hand, from outside.
- A config module `area` with `required`, off by default; `lym area start` refuses on any failure and never falls back to an unsandboxed start.
- Ubuntu 24.04 needs a one-time AppArmor profile for `/usr/bin/bwrap`, loaded by root; the report names the profile, and Ubuntu 25.04 and later ship it, which is not verified on Neve.

This closes the two exposures above and shows early whether tmux, creel and dobby run well inside an area.

### Stop: the operator decides whether stage 1 works well enough to go on.

### Stage 2: egress through a host proxy

No network inside the area; a host-side proxy, reached through a bound socket, allows CONNECT to `api.anthropic.com`, `claude.ai`, `platform.claude.com`, `proxy.golang.org`, `sum.golang.org`, `github.com` and `api.github.com`, with a loopback relay inside the area.
Telemetry and the auto-updater are off by environment.
The GitHub token handed to the area is fine-grained and limited to the hub's repositories; the operator's `gh` login never enters.
WebFetch and the `prowler` skill reach only these hosts.

### Stage 3: a broker for the remaining exits

A host-side process serving a fixed set of verbs and never a command line from the area: the landing deploy (it fetches `origin/main` into its own clone, checks the commit is the tip, builds with the host's Go and installs), `lym reed window` opening Konsole, and `lym hibernate request`.
`lym ide` is refused, since VS Code on the host would run git over repositories the area writes; the host runs no git over the area's repositories at all.

## What is not claimed

Isolation from a kernel exploit, which needs a virtual machine; that data in the area cannot leave through an allowed host; and that a landed change of lym itself cannot run on the host once deployed, which matters on this hub because it develops lym.
Landlock stays a possible inner layer once both machines run a kernel with ABI 9 and 10, and Claude Code deny rules in shuttle's settings are a cheap second line inside the area; the dedicated user, podman, systemd sandboxing and Claude Code's `/sandbox` inside lym runs are left out.
The report estimates the whole at five tasks and eighteen cards.

## Related

Note `creel-cross-hub-mail`: the inbox folder sits outside an area, so reading and writing it goes through the broker.

entries.title: Measure what Cortex XDR costs the test suites on OSL-1046
entries.brief: The 242 s fabricengine tier 1 against 37 to 41 s elsewhere is a machine difference no report has split
entries.body:
## Seen (operator, 2026-11-09)

Cortex XDR on OSL-1046 holds each new binary for about 10 s and scans each file a test creates, and fabricengine tests create many.
The shard report (`docs/research/speed/fabricengine-shards-2026-11-09/report.md`) put the 242 s one-process wall down to load, but the 2026-11-08 figure of 37 to 41 s was measured on another machine, so the gap is machine and Cortex, not load.
The package used 1.23 cores of 16 and `pmd` and `piud` were busy in nearly every sample.

## Idea

Separate the Cortex cost from the rest: the time a freshly built test binary waits before it runs, the time file creation takes with and without a scanned folder, and the fabricengine tier 1 wall with the repository and temp folders excluded from the scan, if the operator can have that changed.
The result says whether to cut tests, cut file and binary creation, or ask for an exclusion.

entries.title: Study whether the hardener finds and fixes real faults
entries.brief: Judge the two fabric hardener campaigns from their records: real findings, sound fixes, focus kept, cost
entries.body:
## Goal

Find out whether the hardener recipe does what it is for: drive the modules its focus names, find real faults, fix them with tests that hold, and converge.

## Evidence

- The first fabric campaign, `harden-fabricengine`, landed as `37649c772` after three rounds.
- The second, `harden-fabric-single-repo-verbs`, the one-repository fabric campaign with the fabric verbs in its sandbox, has landed as `2722a66ef`, so both campaigns are judged.
- The second campaign ran with the model rotation the template then set (opus, fable, sonnet).
  Hardener rounds now default to `sonnet[high]` alone, and a rotation is set per run through `hardener.reviewer` and `hardener.fixer` (`a66d41345`), so judge the rotation's cost and effect against that change.
- The five faults the second campaign found but could not raise are the task `harden-fabric-undriven-cases`.
- Each campaign's round files are under its records worktree at `_lym/reviews/harden/`: `round-<n>-focus.md`, `round-<n>-review.md`, `round-<n>-acceptance.md`, `round-<n>-usage.yaml` and the snapshots, beside its decision record and the landed commits.

## Questions

- **Findings**: for each finding, is it a real fault, a false positive or a matter of taste? Do its repro steps show it?
- **Fixes**: does each fix cure its finding? Does its regression test fail with the fix broken, as the fix rules demand? Was the package doc updated?
- **Focus**: did each round stay inside the campaign's focus? Did the focus files steer later rounds to what was left unverified?
- **Convergence**: did the Bouncer end the campaign on a sound verdict? Were deferred findings filed as open risks and on the board?
- **Misses**: which faults in the same code turned up after the campaign landed, outside it (such as the killed-seed way forward in `0e4782373` and the fetch prune in `f660ac101`), and could the campaign have reached them?
- **Cost**: tokens and wall time per round, from the usage files and the run's records.
- **Seen in the second campaign**: round 2's reviewer recorded smaller faults (O1 to O6) only as prose, since an incremental round admits only BLOCKING findings on changed hunks.
  Round 3's reviewer (sonnet, medium, 4 min) approved with half its focus undriven: the killed discard, the keep-local tag push, a failed step with no kill, and `adopt --archives` over real owner tags.
  A settled harden segment cannot be reopened (`lym loom goto` refuses), so the orch had no way to order another round. Judge each of these, and whether the remaining focus should block approval.
  Round 4 again raised what it found outside the incremental scope only as prose; those are the O1 to O5 of `harden-fabric-undriven-cases`.
  A suspected cause is the stencils, not the model: `contracts/stencils/harden/harden-rubric-review.md` asks for OK, WARN or FAIL on every focus entry,
  while `contracts/stencils/burler/burler-review-format.md` lets an incremental round raise only BLOCKING findings on changed hunks, so such a round can only approve. Judge that conflict.
  Since `8cf7f4775`, a later hardener round cannot approve with its focus undriven:
  the reviewer raises a `decision`-class, BLOCKING, `origin: focus` finding for each focus entry it left undriven or marked WARN,
  `burlerengine.CheckReviewRound` exempts it from the changed-file rule, and the arbiter and then the parent rule on it.
  That answers whether the remaining focus should block approval going forward; judge the campaign's rounds as they ran, and whether the new finding is enough for the rubric conflict.

## Bounds

- Mostly a study of records and commits.
- At most three findings are reproduced, on a sandbox hub against the commit before their fix, one try each; no other trial runs.
- The report ends with a verdict and a short list of concrete changes to the hardener recipe or its stencils, each a candidate note.

entries.title: Fix the five fabric faults the one-repository hardener found but could not raise
entries.brief: Killed clone has no working way forward; merge skips the layout read; kept local tags pushed silently; legacy plain tags unnamed; discard re-run names no command
entries.body:
## Seen

`harden-fabric-single-repo-verbs` round 4 drove the cases round 3 left undriven and approved, but could raise none of what it found as a finding:
its incremental scope held only round 3's gate fix (`internal/gatecli`, `internal/gateslot`, `internal/loomcli`), and an incremental round admits only BLOCKING findings on changed hunks.
It recorded them as observations; they are copied below from `round-4-review.md` in the run's archived records.

- **O1 — MEDIUM, design, CONFIRMED.**
  Location: `internal/fabriccli/fabric.go:673` (the reconcile verb's `NewBolt(boltDir).PullThenCommitWritten`), with `internal/fabricengine/clone.go:225` and `:264` ("hub already exists").
  Scenario (P8, twice): `lym fabric clone <url> --into <dir>` killed once its records store exists and before `_bolt` does.
  `fabric status` and `fabric pull` then print `not initialized here; run "lym fabric reconcile"`;
  typed, `lym fabric reconcile` fails with the raw `gitrepo: git dir of …/_bolt: dotgit: not a git repository …`;
  a plain re-clone answers `hub already exists at …` with no way forward. Only `lym fabric clone <url> --into <dir> --reset`, which no output names, rebuilds the hub.
  Fix: in the reconcile verb, before the Bolt pull, refuse a hub whose `BoltDir` holds no repository with a way forward naming `lym fabric clone <url> --into <parent of the hub> --reset`.
  Make `CloneHub`'s "hub already exists at %s" name the same `--reset` re-run.
  Add a regression test that removes `_bolt` from a hubforge one-repository hub and asserts both messages.
- **O2 — LOW, scope, CONFIRMED.**
  Location: `internal/fabricengine/mergeguards.go:57`.
  Scenario (P7): records store's `remote.origin.fetch` unset; `lym fabric merge y1` stages the merge with `ok: true` and names no layout gap,
  so the weft SHA in the merge record comes from stale tracking refs. Every other verb driven names fabric's refspec way forward.
  Fix: call `originNamespaceAt(f.records path)` before `f.records.Fetch()` in `resolveMergeSources` and log its error with the weft fetch's warning, or return it as the verb's refusal.
  The same gap stands on non-fabric paths: `pull.go:186` and `recordsgit.go:346` via `FastForwardPair`, `codetipsettle.go:21,43` via `DobbyRuns`, `bolt.go:162` via `lym machine name`.
- **O3 — LOW, design, CONFIRMED.**
  Location: `internal/fabricengine/archive.go:294` (`pushLocalArchiveTags`).
  Scenario (P3): a records commit kept under a local `archive/t4/<sha>` tag, as `DropLocal` keeps one with "the tags stay local", is pushed to origin by a later `lym fabric remove t4 --remote`.
  No verb output names the push (the job is handed off), and `lym fabric remove --help` says nothing of it.
  Fix: decide whether `DropLocal`'s tags may leave the machine.
  If yes, name in `lym fabric remove --help` and `cleanup --help` that `--remote` pushes the slug's local archive tags origin lacks, and correct `DropLocal`'s doc.
  If no, give `DropLocal`'s tags a prefix `pushLocalArchiveTags` does not list.
- **O4 — LOW, scope, CONFIRMED.**
  Location: `internal/fabricengine/cleanupremotewarp.go:302` (`remoteTagRefs`, the records-side archive listing `cleanup` reads).
  Scenario (P5): an earlier binary's plain `refs/tags/archive/t5/<sha>` on a one-repository origin is named by no `status`, `cleanup`, `prune` or `reconcile` output, before or after the branch is discarded.
  No commit is lost: the discard pushes its own namespaced tag first.
  Fix: in `cleanup`'s read of a one-repository origin, list plain `refs/tags/archive/*` and `refs/tags/archive-owner/*` refs and report each with a way forward that pushes it under `refs/lym/code-tags/` and deletes the plain ref.
- **O5 — NIT, consistency, CONFIRMED.**
  Location: `internal/fabricengine/remoteteardown.go:187` (`discardRerunWayForward`).
  Scenario (P1): a killed discard's record names "run the command that discarded the task branch again", no command an operator can type; the re-run that works is `lym batten cancel <slug> --remove`.
  Fix: carry the discarding command in the job and the pending record, as the removal and cleanup kinds name theirs, and print it.

Not driven in round 4: the owner-archive push path, the hand-over and code-tip reset paths, and a lease that loses.

## Idea

Fix O1 to O5 as each proposes; for O3, the operator decides whether a tag `DropLocal` keeps may leave the machine.

entries.title: Config keys nest under the area they govern, named with dots
entries.brief: loom.yaml spells the area into flat key names (discussion_review_ask_parent, code_max_bounces); nest them as discussion.review_ask_parent
entries.body:
## Seen

`loom.yaml` holds its keys flat with the area spelled into each name: 19 start `discussion_`, 13 `code_`, 8 `split_`, 3 `pr_`, and more.
Elsewhere a key is named bare without its file, such as `judge_ask_parent` in `drift.yaml`, which reads like the Bouncer's judge of a perch.
T11's change description and halt notices name keys this way, so a reader cannot tell which area a key governs.

## Wanted

Operator, 2026-11-23: a key's name shows the area it sits in, with a dot per level, as `drift.judge_ask_parent` and `loom.discussion.review_ask_parent`.

- `loom.yaml`'s prefixed keys become maps per area: `discussion`, `code`, `split`, `pr` and the others, such as `discussion.review_ask_parent` and `code.max_bounces`.
- `run_settings`, profiles, `lym config --set`, every template comment, doc, stencil and halt notice use the dotted full name, file included.
- Existing hub layers and board `run_settings` are carried over by a reinterpretation, as other key moves were.
- Decide which other templates have flat prefixed keys that belong in the same change.

entries.title: Board view lists a done beam-project task under P0
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #188](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/188).

Seen: lym board list --text showed a task that had landed in a beam project under P0, the root project, instead of under its beam.

Workaround: none; the entry was left until prune.

Expected: a done task stays listed under its own project until it is pruned.

entries.title: Run agents ask a question and exit before the reply; drift judge asks in its pane
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #186](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/186).

Seen: on a loom run, the recovery agent and the code fixer each mailed the parent orch a question and ended their session before the reply arrived; the reply came back from creel as returned. The drift judge instead put its question in its own pane, where no notice reaches the orch, and the run sat waiting until the operator noticed.

Workaround: the orch watched the run's idle panes and answered by creel mail; the returned replies were dropped, and the runs went on without them.

Expected: an agent that asks with --expect-reply waits for the reply before it ends, and every run agent, the drift judge included, asks its parent by creel mail rather than in its pane.

entries.title: tools/godocreflow worsens wrapped-break findings instead of clearing them
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #183](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/183).

What happened: `tools/godocreflow` was run over trimmed Go files to clear 624 wrapped-break findings from `lym loom lint-comments`.
Findings rose to 916.
It skips whole comment blocks that hold a heading or list, and it joins lines past the length limit.
The commit was dropped and the findings were fixed by hand.

Why abnormal: the reflow tool is meant to fix these findings and produced more of them.

What to do: make godocreflow process blocks with headings or lists, and make it respect the line length limit, or stop pointing at it as a fix.

Provenance: task doc-go-trim-pass; note Darn-Write.md.

entries.title: lym loom lint-comments --base checks committed HEAD, not the working tree
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #182](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/182).

What happened: `lym loom lint-comments --base` reads committed HEAD, not the working tree.
A fix to a flagged comment could be verified only after committing it.

Why abnormal: a lint run during editing gives no feedback on uncommitted changes, which forces a commit per check cycle.

What to do: lint the working tree, or add a flag that does, or document the HEAD-only behaviour in the verb's help.

Provenance: task doc-go-trim-pass; note Darn-Write.md.

entries.title: Decision record written with a CLI error envelope as its Goal
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #181](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/181).

A Darn-Write session found the decision record's `## Goal` holding `{"error":"invalid json: invalid character 'h' ...","ok":false}` where the board body belongs, followed only by the triage section.
The task's own text was missing, so the agent rebuilt the scope from the linked issues and triage notes, and the parent's added decision confirmed it.

This is abnormal: a lym verb's error envelope was rendered into the record as if it were the Goal, and nothing refused it before Discussion.
The record writer (Record-Write) should refuse, or fail the run, when the Goal body is a CLI error envelope or otherwise not the board body; the upstream step that fed it the error should also be traced.

Provenance: task slug `halt-escalation-messages`; note file `Darn-Write.md`.

entries.title: Landing blames the token when the branch-rules read returns a plan-limit 403
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #179](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/179).

## What happened

`lym loom` halted `blocked` at the Finalize step with anomaly `escalation-to-human`.
The landing step reads the parent branch's rules through `GET /repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/main?per_page=100`.
GitHub answered 403 with the message "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature."
lym's landing stop reported it as a refused token:

```
landing stop: GitHub refused the token for the call to read GitHub's rules for the parent branch: pullrequest: read the rules active on branch main: GET https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/main?per_page=100: 403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature. []; way forward: make sure the gh user's token (GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, or gh auth login --hostname github.com) is valid and can reach the repository, then run lym loom resume
```

Every earlier step (Preflight through PR-Review) was done or skipped cleanly; the run stopped only at landing.

## Why it is abnormal

The 403 is a plan limitation, not a token problem.
The token is valid and reached the repository; the branch-rules feature is unavailable for a private repository on a free plan.
The way forward lym prints (check the token, then `lym loom resume`) cannot succeed, so the run stays blocked on a loop the operator cannot escape from that advice.
A repository with no rules feature has no rules to enforce, so landing should not need this read to succeed.

## What to do

- Distinguish the 403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public" response from a token refusal in the pullrequest rules read.
- Treat that response as "no active rules" and continue landing, possibly with a note, or
- stop with a way forward that names the plan limitation (use a public repository, upgrade the plan, or opt out of the rules read) instead of the token advice.

Provenance: task `greet-goodbye`, from note `loom-halt.md`.


## From issue #180

Imported from [issue #180](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/180).

## Seen

A darn task run in a hub whose repository is private, on a GitHub free plan, halted at Finalize with this batten notice:

> landing stop: GitHub refused the token for the call to read GitHub's rules for the parent branch: pullrequest: read the rules active on branch main: GET https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/main

GitHub answers that call with `403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature.`
The same `gh` token, which has the `repo` scope, gets the same 403 by hand, and `X-Accepted-Oauth-Scopes` asks only for `repo`.
The token is valid; the endpoint is plan-gated for private repositories.

Moments later the run moved past Finalize to Friction-Reflect and landed with no orch action, so the stop did not hold.

## Expected

Finalize reads this plan-gated 403 as "no readable branch rules" and goes on without a stop.
At the least, the message names the plan gate instead of a refused token,
since its way forward, re-auth and `lym loom resume`, cannot help.

## Workaround

None needed this time: the run went on by itself.

entries.title: Find who pushes weft main outside the board push lock
entries.brief: Board pushes of loomyard-weft refs/heads/main fail with cannot lock ref four times in a row while several runs start
entries.body:
## Goal

Find why pushes of the weft repository's `main`, the board, race each other on one machine, and name the fix.

## Seen

On 2026-11-23 around 09:20, with several runs starting at once on Neve:

- The Bolt checkout's board push failed: `git push https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard-weft.git refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main` was refused with `cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main': is at 9f73b6e9 but expected f4a24e2b`, and `gitrepo` gave up after 4 attempts.
- A `lym batten run` catch-up minutes before logged the same refusal on `ref=main`, beside a records push to `loomyard-weft`.
- A start was refused with `push lock busy: .../loomyard-weft/.weft/fabric.push.lock still held after 30s`.
- `lym board sync` then pushed cleanly.

By design, board writes take the board write lock and every push of the board goes through `coalescePush` under the absorbing `board.push.lock` (`internal/fabricengine/coalesce.go`, `bolt.go`), so one process pushes the latest commit for all waiting writers.
A refusal whose ref moved between read and push means a second pusher of weft `main` acts outside that lock, or under another lock.

## Questions

- Which code paths push weft `main`: list every call site, the lock each takes (`board.push.lock`, `fabric.push.lock` or none), and from which checkout (the Bolt checkout, `loomyard-weft`, a task's records worktree).
- Which of them ran at 09:15 to 09:25 on 2026-11-23, from the hub log and the runs' traces.
- Whether another machine wrote the board in that window.
- Why the retry gives up: does each retry re-read origin and rebase or merge, or push the same stale commit again?

## Bounds

- Read code, logs, traces and git history; no timed runs and no trials.
- The report ends with the cause and a concrete fix for each path, so every push of weft `main` on a machine is coalesced under one lock, as a candidate note.

entries.title: RC button shows green while Remote Control is disabled by organization policy
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #189](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/189).

## Seen

In the DrillOpPlan hub (lym build 30ed1ee58802), the RC button of the orch pane shows green, as if Remote Control were on.
Remote Control is off: the organization's policy disables it, and `/remote-control` in the same session answers "Remote Control is disabled by your organization's policy."
The hub's `orch.yaml` sets no `remote_control`, and after this build its default is off, as the reconcile notice said.

Clicking the button makes reed answer that Remote Control is already on, which it is not (operator, 2026-11-23).

## Expected

The RC button shows Remote Control's real state for the session.
Where the organization's policy disables Remote Control, the button shows it off or unavailable, and a click does not claim it is on.

## Workaround

None needed: the operator ignores the button.

entries.title: Verify-budget notice names no run
entries.body:
## Seen

The orch got creel mail #2450 from `ly:LOOM` (2026-11-23):
"Darn-Write gate: the verify gate has run past its 30m0s budget and is at attempt 3; it goes on until its attempts are spent; no verify run has failed yet".
Neither the sender nor the text names the run, and three darn runs were in Darn-Write at the time,
so the orch could only guess which run it meant.
The line is built by `verifyBudgetNotice` in `internal/loomshed/verifybudget.go`, which takes the gate site but no slug.

## Idea

Put the run's slug in the line, as other parent notices do, so the parent knows which run it is about without a status read.

entries.title: Preflight worktree-clean blocks on lym's own _lym/usage session record
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #190](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/190).

## Seen

A darn run blocked at Preflight on its first step.
The worktree-clean precondition reported `?? _lym/usage/session-<id>.json`, the usage record of one of lym's own sessions, as an uncommitted state change.
The driver's tackler handed the stop back to the parent orch, asking whether to commit the record or to ignore `_lym/usage`.

By the time the orch looked, loom's own `loom: commit run records` commit had committed that record, so `_lym` was clean.
The usage record had been written between loom's records commit and the worktree-clean check.

Stop reason, verbatim:

```
preconditions not met: worktree-clean: uncommitted state changes under `_lym`: ?? _lym/usage/session-db065ed3-54e1-4008-bacd-df683191b516.json; way forward: commit or stash the code changes with git, and commit the _lym changes with `lym fabric commit`, then re-step
```

## Workaround

The orch checked that the record was tracked and `_lym` was clean, then ran `lym loom resume` in the task worktree.
The run's tackler could neither commit nor decide, so the run waited for a parent turn.

## Expected

lym's own usage records never block worktree-clean.
Either worktree-clean leaves out `_lym/usage`, or lym commits the usage records before it runs the check.


## From issue #194

Imported from [issue #194](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/194).

Preflight halts a run as `blocked` because lym's own per-session usage file leaves the worktree dirty.

What happened:
The loom run halted twice at Preflight, anomaly `escalation-to-human`, with this reason (the session id differs between the two halts):

```
preconditions not met: worktree-clean: uncommitted state changes under `_lym`: ?? _lym/usage/session-<id>.json; way forward: commit or stash the code changes with git, and commit the _lym changes with `lym fabric commit`, then re-step; a session lym refuses the verb from reports status: FAILED and the orch runs it
```

The only dirty path is an untracked `_lym/usage/session-<id>.json`, which lym itself wrote for the session that stepped the run.
No code change or agent edit was involved.

Why it is abnormal:
The `worktree-clean` precondition is tripped by lym's own bookkeeping, so a fresh step can block before any work starts.
The way forward asks the session to run `lym fabric commit`, but the same message says a session whose verb lym refuses must report `status: FAILED` and leave it to the orch.
The run therefore escalates to a human for a state lym created.

What to do:
Either exclude `_lym/usage/` from the `worktree-clean` check (or git-ignore it), or have lym commit or flush the usage file before Preflight evaluates the worktree.

Provenance: task `models-wemod-robustness-sanity`; notes `loom-halt.md`, `loom-halt-2.md`.

entries.title: Red-first gate holds every run in a hub whose test scoper is not go
entries.body:
Imported from [issue #192](https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/192).

Seen in a C# hub (NORCE Models), darn run hydraulics-gaps: the red-first gate held the writer's handoff because it cannot run the diff's tests on the merge base when the hub's scoper is not go. The run went on only after the parent orch recorded a decision titled 'No test seam ...' by lym loom decision add, waiving the check. Workaround: the parent records a 'No test seam' decision naming why the check cannot run. Expected: in a hub whose scoper cannot run tests on the merge base, the gate skips red-first or runs it through the hub's own test command, instead of halting every run for a manual waiver.

entries.title: Intake checks whether an issue is already fixed before it reaches the board
entries.body:
## Seen

On 2026-11-23 three imported bugs ran as darn tasks and each found the fault already fixed on the base:
`pr-findings-open-fabric-nil` (fixed by `6fa7f1740`), `amend-plan-loses-webster-batches` (no losing path left) and `rules-read-plan-gated-403` (fixed by `895eab670` two days before).
Each took a run slot in a full queue for nothing.

## Wanted

Operator decision (2026-11-23): board intake checks whether a bug is already fixed before it puts it on the board.

- The intake fork's rules, `contracts/orchrole/role-intake.md`, gain a fourth outcome beside new note, fold and close as noise:
  close as already fixed, its reason naming the commit on `main` that fixed it and how the fork saw it.
- The fork judges it from the code on `main` and its history, as the three runs above did in their first minutes:
  the code path the issue names, and commits since the issue's build that touch it.
- When it cannot tell, the issue goes on the board as now.
- `lym board intake close` may need a reason form that names the fixing commit; decide in the run.
